evaluations.label: A
errors: Names wrong or made up: 'Mark Knopp' (no surname was given), 'Xavier Juukens' (Juergens), 'Dirk Mankveld' (Meinfeld)
Action item 'Mark Knopp - Provide personal assignments to team members': the transcript says the personal coach gives the assignments, not Mark
Action item 'Xavier - Address material considerations for lightweight design' was never assigned; Xavier only said the material should be light
Action item 'User Interface Designer - Prepare intuitive design concepts' was never assigned
'Dolphin: freedom, smooth design': nobody linked 'smooth design' to the dolphin
Several timestamps are off (for example product scope at 10:34, when it was discussed around 11:25-11:34)
strengths: Covers the main topics: brief, three phases, whiteboard, animals, scope, accessibility, light material, price figures
Gets the price numbers right and notes the tight margin
weaknesses: Action items are largely invented or given to the wrong person
Wrong surnames make the notes look unreliable
Very terse bullets with little context

evaluations.label: B
errors: Names wrong or made up: 'Mark Knopf' (no surname was given), 'Dirk Mengveld' (Meinfeld), 'Xavier Jökens' (Juergens)
'UI designer also present (name not captured)': he introduced himself as Nick Broer
'stick to what users are familiar with, rational changes only' reads too much into a garbled line (the transcript says 'No rational changes... revolutionary changes, yes')
strengths: Correctly says assignments come from the personal coach and the next meeting is in 30 minutes
Clear list of the Industrial Designer's three questions and the early design considerations (TV only, intuitive, accessibility, light material, tight budget)
Short, well organized and easy to scan
weaknesses: No explicit action items; misses that Dirk will share his marketing ideas later
Leaves out the UI designer's name and that he said the budget was not much to work with

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'TS3012a' project code does not appear in the transcript
Project Manager called 'Markoff' (he said 'Mark'); 'Savier'/'Savier Jokins' and 'Dirk Mangfelt' are wrong names; UI designer only called 'Speaker 4' though he gave his name
'Speaker 4 clarifies that the scope of the project is limited to a TV remote control': the UI designer asked the question and the Project Manager answered it
Lists 'multi-remote control or limited strictly to television functions?' as an open question, though it was settled as TV only
'lightweight materials that are aesthetically impactful': nobody said aesthetically impactful
strengths: Detailed outline covering intros, goals, smart board training, the animal exercise, product constraints and next steps
weaknesses: Action items have no owners and are generic
Wrong attribution, and the TV-only decision is shown as still open
Repeats itself across Summary and Outline; misses that the personal coach gives the assignments and that Dirk will share ideas later

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'Dirk Mengveld' in the action item (his name is Dirk Meinfeld)
'They set a €25 selling price': the Project Manager handed the team these targets; the team did not set them
'The interface designer urged familiarity and rational changes' reads too much into a garbled line
strengths: Says who said what correctly: the PM confirmed TV only, the UI designer raised accessibility, Xavier asked for light material, the UI designer said the budget was not much to work with
Correctly says the personal coach gives the assignments and the team meets again in 30 minutes
Records that Dirk has marketing ideas to share later, with an owner
Clear verdict-first sections with timestamps; someone who missed the meeting could follow it
weaknesses: Leaves out the UI designer's name and the Industrial Designer's three questions
Only one action item (accurate, but thin)

rationale: D is the most accurate. It says correctly who said what, who hands out assignments (the personal coach), and that Dirk will share marketing ideas later, and it has only small name and wording slips. B is accurate and well organized but has no action items and gets some surnames wrong. A covers the topics but makes up most of its action items, gives the assignment of work to Mark instead of the coach, and gets the names wrong. C invents a project code, misnames the Project Manager, says the UI designer settled the scope, lists the settled TV-only question as open, and gives action items without owners.
